messages:
Molly (marketing): Heads-up — we need a quick iteration on our competitive battlecards for the April webinar / benchmark post. Focus: cloud AI platforms, LLM API players, and infra vendors. TL;DR: sales wants crisp callouts + routing rules for inbound leads.
Jamal (gTM): +1. Priorities: AWS/GCP managed endpoints, Anthropic/OpenAI APIs, and Replicate/Runway style infra vendors. Sales questions: pricing delta, SLO guarantees, and on-prem options.
Sofia (content): I can draft three narrative hooks: 1) "predictable economics" vs cloud AI (latency/cost table), 2) "unified runtime" vs LLM APIs (dev DX), 3) "deploy anywhere" vs infra vendors (private install checklist). Want to pair with a one-slide battlecard per competitor.
Grant (sales-eng): Make sure each card has:"Key objection", "Suggested response", "Deal signal (why Redwood)" and "Routing rule". Eg objection: "We already use Vendor X's managed endpoints" -> response: "If you need strict latency SLOs and deterministic unit cost, Redwood offers Dedicated pools + SLA".
Tia (product): For the benchmark narrative: can we commit to a single microbenchmark dataset and a latency/cost matrix we can publish? Need approval from infra to run. Also flagged: don't publish token-level pricing comparisons without legal sign-off.
Molly (marketing): Good call. Action plan: Sofia -> draft cards + two-sentence narrative per competitor by EOD Thu (1711084800). Jamal -> add routing heuristics for inbound leads (which competitor mention => route to AE tier or SDR). Grant -> compile top 5 sales objections and one-liners. Tia -> confirm benchmark suite and legal constraints. I'll coordinate final review with product + sales.
Sofia (content): Starting outline now. Quick sample for OpenAI vs Redwood: 
```
Objection: "OpenAI has best models + streaming"
Response: "OpenAI models are strong; Redwood focuses on serving predictability: pinned versions, KV caching, and Dedicated throughput that limits tail-latency variance. We also offer private deployments for regulated data."
Why Redwood: "Predictable latency, cost controls, and private options to meet compliance."
Routing: if prospect mentions pricing or latency SLA -> route to AE (mid-market/enterprise).
```
Grant (sales-eng): Love it. For infra vendors (e.g., Replicate-like): objection: "We self-host; we don't need a managed stack" -> response: "If your team wants to avoid ops complexity and get consistent perf across GPUs and quantization configs, Redwood reduces TCO and gives rollout tools + observability." Also: add a checkbox for "requires air-gapped/on-prem" to surface to sales.
Molly (marketing): One more thing — can we include a small playbook snippet for inbound routing? Jamal, can you paste the proposed rule set here (example format ok)?
Jamal (gTM): Putting a simple routing snippet: 
```
if message contains ["OpenAI", "gpt-4", "API"] and mentions "SLA" or "latency": route -> AE-enterprise
if message contains ["Replicate","self-host","on-prem"]: route -> Solutions-Eng + AE
if message mentions "cost per token" or "pricing": route -> SDR + pricing sheet link
```
Molly (marketing): Perfect. I'll fold that into the battlecard footer and add a short CTA for webinar signups. Can we lock owners? Sofia (owner content), Grant (owner sales objections), Jamal (routing rules), Tia (benchmarks). Final review next Tue sync (1711100000).
deploy-bot: Note: doc created: https://drive.redwood/examples/battlecard-drafts (permission: marketing/view).
Molly (marketing): Thanks everyone — small, actionable iteration. I'll ping legal on the pricing wording. :thumbsup:
